question.problem: Expressed as a mixed number in its lowest terms, $1\,\frac{1}{7}\times 1\,\frac{1}{6}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we write $1\,\frac{1}{7}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{1}{7}=\frac{(1\times 7)+1}{7}=\frac{8}{7}
$$

We also write $1\,\frac{1}{6}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{1}{6}=\frac{(1\times 6)+1}{6}=\frac{7}{6}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{7}\times \frac{7}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{7}\times \frac{7}{6} & =\frac{8}{6}\times \frac{7}{7} \\  & =\frac{8}{6}\times 1 \\  & =\frac{8}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we write this fraction in its lowest terms:

$$
\frac{8}{6}=\frac{8÷2}{6÷2}=\frac{4}{3}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{4}{3}=1\,\text{R}3=1\,\frac{1}{3}
$$
